authorization: Bearer token issued by another tool's local runtime; user-authorized flow required
origin: structure documented; the message string is SYNTHETIC
notes: HTTP 200 and envelope code 0, but data.kind is 'error': an upstream failure does not fail the envelope and is returned in band. status is the upstream HTTP status when the local server knows it, and is optional. A parser that checks only the transport status and the envelope code would treat this as a successful quota read and find no quota, which must not become a zero or a Missing-without-reason row. The message text is invented; only the kind / message / status contract is documented. Every JSON response from this server is wrapped in {code, msg, data, request_id} and the HTTP status is almost always 200, so the business result is code (0 = success) and must be checked before data. Some error envelopes carry non-empty data, which is why checking the status line or the presence of data first is wrong. request_id is an invented 26-character ULID-shaped string. The server binds plain HTTP on loopback (127.0.0.1:58627 by default) and requires a bearer token for every /api/* path except the liveness probe; that token belongs to another tool's runtime and must never be captured, stored or committed. The whole API is documented as experimental: endpoints, fields and event types may change in any version, so the /openapi.json served by the version actually in use has to be re-validated at runtime before any of these shapes is trusted.
